title: Iterative linear quadratic regulator on SU(N) for multi-qubit gate synthesis
authors: Dirk Heimann, Felix Wiebe, Elie Mounzer, Shivesh Kumar
abstract: In quantum optimal control theory, gradient-based trajectory optimization techniques have proven versatile in designing multi-qubit quantum gates. Furthermore, incorporating the underlying Lie-group structure can accelerate the optimization process. In this work, we adapt the Lie-group formulation of the iterative linear quadratic regulator (iLQR) to the special unitary group SU(N) and apply it to quantum gate synthesis, systematically comparing it against the standard Euclidean iLQR formulation across multiple two- to five-qubit gates. We find that in the idealized, unconstrained setting, where all Lie-algebra basis elements are available as drive Hamiltonian terms, the Lie-group formulation converges faster than the Euclidean iLQR formulation. If drive terms are constrained to 2-local Hamiltonian terms, the Lie-group variant converges faster in early optimization iterations, but exhibits greater sensitivity to initialization and a stronger tendency towards local minima. These results demonstrate that incorporating Lie-group geometry into iLQR substantially improves convergence and highlight important next steps for improvements in constrained control settings.
summary: This paper develops and applies an adaptation of the Iterative Linear Quadratic Regulator (iLQR) tailored specifically to the Lie-group structure of SU(N). By incorporating this geometric constraint into the optimization process, the authors demonstrate improved convergence speed for quantum gate synthesis compared to standard methods. The findings highlight the value of group theory in enhancing optimal control algorithms for multi-qubit systems.
main_problem: The primary goal is designing complex multi-qubit quantum gates using Quantum Optimal Control (QOC) theory.
main_result: Incorporating the Lie-group geometry into the iLQR formulation accelerates convergence compared to Euclidean methods in unconstrained settings, though it increases sensitivity to initialization under constraints.
method: The authors adapt the Iterative Linear Quadratic Regulator (iLQR) by formulating updates and cost functions directly on the Special Unitary group SU(N), comparing this Lie-group approach against standard Euclidean iLQR.
model_or_system: The system involves quantum dynamics evolving on the special unitary group SU(N), where control is achieved by applying time-dependent Hamiltonian terms (drive fields) to synthesize target gates.
key_observables: Convergence speed, gate fidelity, and the resulting infidelities of synthesized gates.
important_parameters: The comparison hinges on two regimes: an idealized unconstrained setting versus a constrained setting limited to 2-local Hamiltonian terms.
main_assumptions: The derivation relies heavily on Taylor expansions and linearizing the system dynamics around the current trajectory, which introduces approximations.
figures_summary: Figures show infidelity results for various multi-qubit gates (e.g., three- and five-qubit gates) comparing performance across different optimization score functions and iteration steps.
paper_structure: The paper builds mathematically by deriving necessary Taylor expansions on Lie groups, detailing the iLQR update equations for SU(N), and then presenting numerical results comparing the convergence of the Lie-group vs. Euclidean formulations under varying constraints.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous mathematical framework for optimizing quantum controls by respecting the underlying group structure (SU(N)), which is crucial for developing scalable, physically constrained gate synthesis protocols.
